title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy option to automatically block identified external bots
summary: The briefing's blocking behaviour, policy controls, default and rollout dates are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement and the feature guide's inconsistent PowerShell examples.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Teams is adding automatic blocking of identified external meeting bots to existing admin controls.
claims.quote: Extending the admin controls provided for managing external AI bots and regulating their access to your meetings, we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and GCC.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Android, Desktop, iOS, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The automatic blocking option is off until an administrator enables it, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Default state: Off. No changes occur unless an administrator enables the policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no action unless the organisation plans to use the capability.
claims.quote: No action is required unless you plan to use this capability.

claims.claim: The supplied notice was updated on 3 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice gives a Targeted Release start in mid-September 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-September 2026 (previously early August)

claims.claim: Targeted Release was expected to complete by late September 2026.
claims.quote: expected to complete by late September 2026 (previously late August)

claims.claim: Worldwide General Availability begins in early October 2026 according to the notice.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 (previously late August)

claims.claim: Worldwide General Availability was expected to complete by the end of November 2026.
claims.quote: expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The notice places the new option in existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: A new policy option will be added to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.
claims.quote: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Enabling the setting prevents identified external meeting bots from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.
claims.quote: Identified external meeting bots will be prevented from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.

claims.claim: Existing detection and visibility experiences remain available when the option is enabled.
claims.quote: Existing bot detection and visibility experiences for organizers and administrators will continue to be available.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Organisations that do not enable the setting retain the current detection experience and unchanged meeting participation behaviour.
claims.quote: Organizations that do not enable this setting will continue to use the current bot detection experience with no change to meeting participation behavior.

claims.claim: The feature guide documents Do not detect bots, When detected, require approval before joining, and Block all detected bots.
claims.quote:
Do not detect bots | AllowBots
When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected
Block all detected bots | BlockDetectedBots

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Do not detect bots leaves bots undetected and unmarked, treating them as other external participants.
claims.quote: Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings and follow the meeting's existing access and lobby settings.

claims.claim: The feature guide calls the detection-disabling value AllowBots.
claims.quote: | Do not detect bots | AllowBots |

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference instead lists AllowAllBots for disabling detection.
claims.quote: AllowAllBots: Don't detect bots; Bots will appear the same as other participants. Standard lobby policies will apply to them.

claims.claim: When detected, require approval before joining, with value RequireApprovalWhenDetected, is the existing setting's default.
claims.quote: | When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected | Detected external bots are placed in the meeting lobby and require explicit approval before joining. |

claims.claim: Under the approval option, detected bots are identified in the lobby and require admission before joining.
claims.quote: Detected bots are placed in the meeting lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration. Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: Block all detected bots maps to BlockDetectedBots and automatically blocks detected bots.
claims.quote: | Block all detected bots | BlockDetectedBots | Detected external bots are automatically blocked from joining meetings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Organisers and other participants cannot admit bots blocked by Block all detected bots.
claims.quote: They can't be admitted by meeting organizers or other participants.

claims.claim: Blocked detected bots are not put in the lobby for organiser approval.
claims.quote: They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval, and meeting organizers can't admit them.

claims.claim: Teams detection uses infrastructural and behavioural signals collected during the join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process. We utilize a combination of infrastructural and behavioral signals

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting assistants may record or transcribe meetings without participants' awareness.
claims.quote:
These bots may:
- Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External bots may store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organisation's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Detection may miss bots, and the blocking option does not guarantee blocking every external bot.
claims.quote: The Block all detected bots option applies to bots identified by Teams detection mechanisms. It does not guarantee that all external bots will be blocked.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Detection may misclassify human participants as bots and automatic blocking may prevent their joining.
claims.quote: Detection may incorrectly identify a human participant as a bot. How these participants can join depends on the configured policy

claims.claim: Where supported, eligible misidentified people can use email verification recovery to verify identity and attempt to join.
claims.quote: Participants incorrectly identified as bots may be prevented from joining the meeting. Where supported, eligible participants can use the email verification recovery experience to verify their identity and attempt to join.

claims.claim: The change adds an access restriction rather than granting new access to automated participants.
claims.quote: we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends evaluating the feature with a pilot group before broader deployment.
claims.quote: Evaluate the feature with a pilot group before broader deployment.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing the organisation's use of meeting bots and automated meeting applications.
claims.quote: Review your organization's use of meeting bots and automated meeting applications.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing existing meeting policies and deciding which users or groups receive the policy.
claims.quote: Review existing Teams meeting policies and determine which users or groups should receive the policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation and help desk guidance as appropriate.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation and help desk guidance as appropriate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends communicating with organisers and users who rely on automated meeting bots.
claims.quote: Communicate the change to meeting organizers and users who rely on automated meeting bots in their workflows.

claims.claim: The setting is a Teams meeting policy control scoped at user or group level.
claims.quote: Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: Admins can configure the tenant default org-wide meeting policy or create or modify a targeted policy for users or groups.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.
claims.quote: The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

claims.claim: The feature guide marks its applicability as meetings, not events.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: [Image of a checkmark for yes] Meetings [Image of a x for no] Events

claims.claim: The setting is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy.
Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode BlockDetectedBots configures automatic blocking.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to Governance controls: 'The feature guide names Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy in its prose but uses Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy in its examples; the linked Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference documents ExternalBotAccessMode and BlockDetectedBots.' The conflicting examples are at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing is recorded as unknown because no feature-specific requirement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and the first Cost and licensing paragraph with: 'A Teams licence is required: Manage Teams licenses states that, except for joining meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation needs a Teams licence before using Teams. No requirement or meter specific to this blocking option is published as of November 2026.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access to sources. Keep the question about a feature-specific Teams Premium requirement.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The external-bots feature guide itself lists no licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: manage external bots role license; external bots Teams licensing Teams Premium. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots in full; it lists no licence prerequisite.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter specific to this automatic blocking option is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams automatically block detected external meeting bots pricing metered license requirement; BlockDetectedBots license meter. Read manage-external-bots and teams-add-on-licensing/licensing-enhance-teams on Learn; neither names a meter for blocking.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice names a licence or meter for the option.
claims.quote: Searched: licence, license, meter, price in the complete supplied notice and roadmap record; neither names a licence or meter.

claims.claim: The feature guide does not state the admin role needed to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched: manage external bots role license. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots in full, including Configure policy in Teams Admin Center; it names no required admin role.

claims.claim: The supplied notice gives no separate GCC rollout schedule.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.claim: Learn asks administrators to report undetected external bots through the Feedback option in Teams.
claims.quote: Help improve the system by reporting any undetected external meeting bots to us via the Feedback option in Teams.

claims.claim: The exact message shown to a blocked participant remains undocumented in the checked material.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Block all detected bots blocked participant message email verification recovery. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots and supplied MC1459141; neither quotes the blocked participant's message.

claims.claim: The change affects meeting policy administrators and organisers and participants in organisations that choose to enable it.
claims.quote: Teams administrators who manage meeting policies and security controls.- Meeting organizers and participants in organizations that choose to enable this policy.
